title: the golden deer
hook: something too beautiful to be real is grazing outside the hut, and only one of the three says so

segments.voice: Yesterday: threatened by his own king, Maricha agreed to go. Better to die by Rama's hand.

Near Panchavati, Maricha changes shape. Valmiki enjoys describing what he becomes: a golden body dotted with silver, horns tipped with jewels, a face of rubies and sapphires, ears like blue lotuses. It wanders near the hut, nibbling leaves, running a little, coming back, lying down nearby as if it had all the time in the world. The other deer of the forest smell something wrong and keep their distance. Sita, out picking flowers, doesn't.
screen: `GOLD, DOTTED WITH SILVER.` → `HORNS TIPPED WITH JEWELS.` → `THE REAL DEER KEEP AWAY.`

segments.voice: Sita calls to Rama and Lakshmana, amazed, and they come. Lakshmana looks for a moment and says it plainly. This is Maricha. Kings who came hunting in this forest have been killed by him in disguise. There's no deer like this anywhere on earth. It's a trick. Sita, the text says, is captivated. She asks Rama to catch it, alive if he can, so they can take it home to Ayodhya when the exile ends and keep it in the palace. If he can't, she says, bring back the golden skin. Rama is captivated too, but not naive. If it's real, he tells Lakshmana, it's a wonder worth having. If you're right and it's Maricha, it's a rakshasa who has killed people, and I should deal with it anyway. Either way, I'll go. Stay here and guard Sita. Don't leave her for a moment. Look how carefully the story sets this up. Nobody is foolish. Lakshmana sees through it. Rama has a reason for each possibility. Sita's wish is one anyone might have: a beautiful thing in a hard place. And still every reasonable choice walks straight into Ravana's plan. Valmiki blames no one yet. He just lets you watch the trap close.
screen: `LAKSHMANA: IT'S MARICHA.` · `CATCH IT, OR BRING THE SKIN.` · `EITHER WAY, I'LL GO.` · `GUARD SITA. DON'T LEAVE HER.` · then, large: `REASONABLE CHOICES, A CLOSING TRAP.`

segments.voice: Think of something shiny you want right now: a purchase, a scroll you can't stop, a plan that looks too good. Picture it golden and bright, and look at it a little longer than usual, noticing what a calm part of you sees. Let the shine fade a little, and come back to the plain, ordinary breath.
The golden deer. Maricha in disguise, too beautiful to be real. Lakshmana sees through it, Sita longs for it, and Rama goes after it.
Your line: the golden deer. Too beautiful to be real, and chased anyway. Day five hundred sixty-eight, done.

howItsDone: The golden deer is a familiar scene in Ramayana painting and performance, and the phrase 'golden deer' is sometimes used for an attractive illusion.

original.note: Sanskrit māyāmṛga: illusion-deer, a name later tellings give the golden deer.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sita foolishly wants a pretty deer.
what it means: everyone has reasons, and the trap works through all of them.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 42–43 give the deer's description, Lakshmana's warning, Sita's request and Rama's two-sided reasoning.

chat.says: If Lakshmana saw through the deer, why did Rama still go after it?
options: Rama reasoned that a real deer was a wonder, and if it was Maricha, he should deal with it.
Rama didn't believe Lakshmana and thought his brother was just jealous of the deer.
Sita refused to speak to Rama until he promised to bring the deer back alive.
chat.meaning: Rama had a reason for each case: a wonder if real, a killer to stop if Maricha. Every reasonable choice walked into the trap.

Maricha.meaning: the rakshasa who takes the shape of the golden deer

Panchavati.meaning: the place of five banyans, where the exiles live

Ayodhya.meaning: Rama's home city, his father's capital

Ravana.meaning: the king of Lanka, whose plan this is
